parsed.explanation: In Step 4(c), $I\cup Z_\omega$ is countable and possibly infinite, so the minimal transversal $T$ produced by Zorn (part (a)'s chain-intersection machinery exists precisely because transversals may be infinite) is a priori possibly infinite; the text obtains finiteness of $T$ only from $T\in\mathcal C$ by (iii) plus members of $\mathcal C$ being finite. Thus the final step applies (iii) to a possibly infinite minimal transversal. Claim 3.2 asserts full self-duality, but its proof forms $\pi(T)=\prod_{p\in T}p$, meaningful only for finite $T$; so it verifies (iii) only for finite minimal transversals. Nowhere else does the text show that every minimal transversal of the actual family $\mathcal C$ is finite (ruling out an infinite minimal transversal is essentially as hard as the finiteness being proved, and is not repaired elsewhere). Step 4 therefore cannot be legitimately applied as written.
